parsed.explanation: State sphere is exceptionally protective: no mapped bathroom ban, shield law for visitors seeking lawful care, public-accommodations and hate-crime protections, and local self-ID facilities. That does not govern the federal gate. National passport binary, X-marker cessation, entry-cable refusal and possible lifetime fraud finding on document discrepancy, federal-facility restriction, and documented severe immigration-custody abuse create a universal, state-run exposure before the protective state regime is reached. Federal hostility and counterterrorism framing compound it; litigation may mitigate but is unresolved.

entry_documents.exposure: National binary-sex passport rule effective after Supreme Court ruling; X/new mismatched markers stopped, existing X valid until expiry. Entry cable: document discrepancy or reasonable doubt requires refusal and more evidence; suspected wilful misrepresentation may support permanent fraud ineligibility, though not automatic and waiver possible. Passports reported confiscated/blocked.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiration. No documented state-level entry protection; state law does not govern national documents.
entry_documents.interaction: Border is first encounter and can strand, refuse or create fraud exposure before any state shield, care or facilities protection operates.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody reports: trans men subjected to forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse, with guards invoking masculinity. Federal corrections model from 2026 described as conversion therapy, hair cutting, hormone removal.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No documented visitor custody safeguard or consular-access protocol. Courts may enjoin some orders, but no documented remedy for custody abuse.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A passport discrepancy at entry can escalate to refusal, investigation or detention, where birth-sex/federal custody practices override state protections.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal executive order bars government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with gender identity. State manner is otherwise favorable: no ban in mapped categories for this jurisdiction.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State anti-discrimination in public accommodations since 2006; single-occupancy public restrooms gender-neutral from 2020; largest city: each person determines own gender identity for bathroom access, all-gender school bathrooms since 2021. May 2023 multi-occupancy bill signing unresolved.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State facilities are protective, but federal buildings, airports and federal custody remain under national restriction; traveller must navigate both systems.

care_services.exposure: National orders label minors' gender-affirming care mutilation, propose barring public insurance under 18, and DOJ subpoenaed hospital records for patients under 19. Proposed rules partly enjoined/unresolved.
care_services.protection: 2023 shield law protects patients and providers from civil/criminal charges where care lawful in this jurisdiction was banned in home jurisdiction, expressly including travellers from outside. Conversion therapy on minors banned since 2016.
care_services.interaction: Shield protects state-level care access for adult and minor visitors, but does not document protection against federal subpoena or investigation; shield withstands outside subpoenas is not sourced.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National government defines sex as binary at birth, orders removal of gender-identity materials/policies, bans trans athletes, directs investigation/prosecution over school gender-ideology/social transition, and 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritizes groups described as radically pro-transgender. State threat-framing absent.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: State hate-crime enhancements for gender identity since 2016, earlier sexual-orientation enhancements, gay/trans panic defence repealed 2018, and gender-identity discrimination bans. National hate-crime statute exists but state coverage figure is pre-2020 in dossier.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal institutions frame trans identity as fraud/security concern while state institutions provide recourse; which actor controls the encounter determines outcome.

minors_guardians.exposure: Federal orders direct law-enforcement investigation of schools promoting gender ideology and criminal prosecution of teachers facilitating a minor's social transition, including names/pronouns. Youth-care bans exist in 27 other jurisdictions and federal insurance bar is proposed.
minors_guardians.protection: Shield law protects patients/providers for care lawful here, including out-of-jurisdiction travellers; state conversion-therapy ban for minors, school bullying protections and 2019 student name/pronoun/dress procedures.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling minor can receive shielded care in-state, but federal school, funding and records actions may still reach providers/guardians; no documented federal immunity.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: National poll: 66% support birth-sex on documents, 69% support athletes competing by birth sex, indicating substantial official-policy-aligned public support but not documented violence prevalence. Hate-crime reporting/prosecution for this jurisdiction not sourced.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State public-accommodations and hate-crime protections, documented as law. No documented pattern of targeted street sweeps in this jurisdiction.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: State law gives recourse for discrimination and bias crime, while national hostility may embolden harassment; absence of violence data is not treated as safety.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport ACLU litigation pending; several executive orders enjoined but status varies by measure and time of travel. Federal refusal remedies described as slow, rarely revised in comparable screening.
remedies_unknowns.protection: State anti-discrimination and hate-crime machinery exists on paper and some orders are blocked/enjoined. Legal-aid FAQ on passport rules documented. Enforcement outcomes for this jurisdiction not sourced.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: State remedies do not cancel federal entry/custody exposure; federal litigation may change rules but cannot be relied on as current protection.

anchor_checks.comparison: Jurisdiction is higher than 0.25-C: no documented routine birth-sex prison placement for ordinary visitors in the state and no local bathroom arrest regime, but federal immigration-custody abuse and entry fraud exposure prevent a low-0.3s rating.

Similar to 0.55-B on entry: discretionary secondary screening and refusal on document discrepancy, with slow/rarely revised remedies. State shield, facilities and public-accommodations protections lift it modestly above that anchor.

Lower than 0.75-C: that anchor accepts passports matching presentation with trained border staff and tribunal relief. Here national policy rejects X/mismatched markers and instructs refusal, so state protections cannot reach the border.

Lower than 0.85-A: state law approaches that protective profile, but national passport, federal-facility, counterterrorism and custody regimes are actively hostile rather than merely imperfectly enforced.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime is bifurcated. Once admitted, the traveller encounters a top-tier protective state: shielded care including for visitors and minors, gender-neutral facilities locally, and discrimination/hate-crime law. The journey, however, begins under a hostile federal gate that can refuse entry, confiscate documents or allege fraud, restricts federal facilities, and can place a detainee in abusive custody. State protections do not pre-empt those federal stages. Net risk is therefore moderate: daily life is comparatively safe, but discovery at entry or in federal custody carries severe, state-run consequences with unresolved federal remedies.
